cards.front: Recall a key point about Technology in Everyday Life
cards.back: This topic covers key vocabulary and structures for technology in everyday life. You need to know the topic vocabulary, be able to use it in all four skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), and express opinions with reasons.

cards.front: What should you know about french exam tips — technology in everyday life?
cards.back: 1. For Technology in Everyday Life, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Technology in Everyday Life, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
smartphone (e.g. Mon smartphone est indispensable — My smartphone is essential)

cards.front: What does les réseaux sociaux mean?
cards.back: social media (e.g. Je passe trop de temps sur les réseaux sociaux — I spend too much time on social media)
to download (e.g. J'ai téléchargé une nouvelle application — I downloaded a new app)

cards.front: What does la fracture numérique mean?
cards.back: digital divide (e.g. La fracture numérique existe entre les villes et les campagnes — The digital divide exists between cities and rural areas)
cyberbullying (e.g. La cyberviolence est un problème grave — Cyberbullying is a serious problem)

cards.front: What does le harcèlement en ligne mean?
cards.back: online harassment (e.g. Le harcèlement en ligne est puni par la loi — Online harassment is punished by law)

cards.front: What does un influenceur / une influenceuse mean?
cards.back: influencer (e.g. Les influenceurs ont un grand impact — Influencers have a big impact)

cards.front: What does la French Tech mean?
cards.back: French Tech (startup initiative) (e.g. La French Tech soutient les startups — French Tech supports startups)
mobile payment service (Africa) (e.g. Orange Money est très utilisé au Sénégal — Orange Money is widely used in Sénégal)

cards.front: What does la fibre optique mean?
cards.back: fibre optic (e.g. La fibre optique est rapide — Fibre optic is fast)
subscription (e.g. J'ai un abonnement Netflix — I have a Netflix subscription)
streaming (e.g. Le streaming est très populaire — Streaming is very popular)

Students often forget to use the perfect tense for completed past activities. Wrong: Hier, je joue au foot. Correct: Hier, j'ai joué au foot (perfect tense for completed past actions). Students also mix up à and en with countries. Wrong: Je vais à France. Correct: Je vais en France (en with feminine countries starting with consonant).
